10First-order condition for the evidence §

For a reference measure ν\nuν, define Zi(a)=∫e−Ui(a,z) dν(z)Z_i(a)=\int e^{-U_i(a,z)}\,d\nu(z)Zi​(a)=∫e−Ui​(a,z)dν(z), πi,a(dz)=Zi(a)−1e−Ui(a,z)ν(dz)\pi_{i,a}(dz)=Z_i(a)^{-1}e^{-U_i(a,z)}\nu(dz)πi,a​(dz)=Zi​(a)−1e−Ui​(a,z)ν(dz), and the averaged log evidence ℓ(a)=M−1∑ilog⁡Zi(a)\ell(a)=M^{-1}\sum_i\log Z_i(a)ℓ(a)=M−1∑i​logZi​(a), where M>0M>0M>0. The normalizers must be positive. Assume the densities are measurable at the point under consideration and almost everywhere strongly measurable for every parameter in some neighbourhood of that point; at the point they are integrable and their weighted gradients are almost everywhere strongly measurable; and on one common parameter neighbourhood the potentials are differentiable almost everywhere and e−Ui(b,z)∥∇bUi(b,z)∥e^{-U_i(b,z)}\|\nabla_bU_i(b,z)\|e−Ui​(b,z)∥∇b​Ui​(b,z)∥ is bounded by an integrable function of zzz. These domination hypotheses justify differentiation under the integral sign.

Claim. If aaa is a local maximizer of ℓ\ellℓ, then ∑i∫∇aUi(a,z) dπi,a(z)=0\sum_i\int\nabla_aU_i(a,z)\,d\pi_{i,a}(z)=0∑i​∫∇a​Ui​(a,z)dπi,a​(z)=0.

Proof. Positivity of Zi(a)Z_i(a)Zi​(a) permits the logarithmic chain rule. Dividing its derivative by Zi(a)Z_i(a)Zi​(a) converts the weighted score integral into a posterior expectation, so ∇ℓ(a)=−M−1∑i∫∇aUi(a,z) dπi,a(z)\nabla\ell(a)=-M^{-1}\sum_i\int\nabla_aU_i(a,z)\,d\pi_{i,a}(z)∇ℓ(a)=−M−1∑i​∫∇a​Ui​(a,z)dπi,a​(z). A differentiable real function on the whole parameter space has zero derivative at a local maximum: for each direction its restriction to a real line has a local maximum at zero, whose derivative is zero. Thus the averaged score vanishes. Since M>0M>0M>0, multiplication by MMM yields the unaveraged identity. Posterior integrability is furnished by the normalizer domination assumptions, rather than inferred from formal cancellation. □\square□

11Euler recursion against a stationary posterior reference §

Use the scaled cloud with K>0K>0K>0, differentiable jointly mmm-strongly convex potentials, and LLL-Lipschitz gradients. Take m,h>0m,h>0m,h>0, mh≤1mh\le1mh≤1, hL2≤mhL^2\le mhL2≤m, and put q=1−mh/2q=1-mh/2q=1−mh/2. All random states lie in L2(P)L^2(P)L2(P), whose norm is (E∥X∥2)1/2(\mathbb E\|X\|^2)^{1/2}(E∥X∥2)1/2, for a probability measure PPP. Supply a continuous stationary frozen-posterior integral solution StS_tSt​, driven by the stated coordinate Brownian processes. Its parameter block at time zero is the constant a⋆a_\stara⋆​. Assume the initial per-particle parameter scores are independent and their expectations sum to zero. These are explicit stochastic and reference assumptions.

Claim. Let QQQ be extraction of the parameter block, with operator norm at most one. Put V=∑iE∥si−Esi∥2V=\sum_i\mathbb E\|s_i-\mathbb Es_i\|^2V=∑i​E∥si​−Esi​∥2, G=∥Ffrozen(S0)∥L2G=\|F_{\rm frozen}(S_0)\|_{L^2}G=∥Ffrozen​(S0​)∥L2​, and let WWW denote the physical Brownian increment scale. The coupled full-batch trajectory satisfies

∥QXn−a⋆∥L2≤qn∥X0−S0∥L2+2mVK+Lm(hG+43Wh).\|QX_n-a_\star\|_{L^2}\le q^n\|X_0-S_0\|_{L^2}+\frac2m\frac{\sqrt V}{K}+\frac Lm\left(hG+\frac43W\sqrt h\right).∥QXn​−a⋆​∥L2​≤qn∥X0​−S0​∥L2​+m2​KV​​+mL​(hG+34​Wh​).

Proof. Write si=(si−Esi)+Esis_i=(s_i-\mathbb Es_i)+\mathbb Es_isi​=(si​−Esi​)+Esi​. The sum of the means vanishes. Expanding the squared norm of their average leaves diagonal terms plus cross inner products. Independence and centring make every cross expectation zero. Consequently the mean-square residual is exactly K−2VK^{-2}VK−2V, whose nonnegative square root is V/K\sqrt V/KV​/K. Stationarity preserves this residual norm at every reference time. The frozen integral equation supplies the reference segments used in the numerical comparison; its drift norm is GGG, and Brownian increments supply the square-root-time scale WWW. Apply the equilibrium-reference Euler comparison with this residual bound. The parameter block of StS_tSt​ is constant. Finally ∥Q(Xn−Snh)∥L2≤∥Xn−Snh∥L2\|Q(X_n-S_{nh})\|_{L^2}\le\|X_n-S_{nh}\|_{L^2}∥Q(Xn​−Snh​)∥L2​≤∥Xn​−Snh​∥L2​ transfers the cloud estimate to the parameter estimate. □\square□

12Mean-field and particle comparisons §

Let the heterogeneous particle potentials be differentiable and jointly mmm-strongly convex, with LLL-Lipschitz gradients, and let the particle count be positive. Consider a continuous L2(P)L^2(P)L2(P) mean-field integral solution YtY_tYt​ and a continuous stationary frozen-posterior solution StS_tSt​ driven by the same physical Brownian path. Assume the posterior scores have zero total expectation, and the initial parameter of YYY and the reference parameter of SSS are deterministic. The statement holds for any real mmm; it gives decay when m>0m>0m>0. Existence of a new solution is not asserted by a comparison of supplied solutions.

Claim. If the reference parameter is a⋆a_\stara⋆​, then for every t≥0t\ge0t≥0, ∥QYt−a⋆∥L2≤e−mt∥Y0−S0∥L2\|QY_t-a_\star\|_{L^2}\le e^{-mt}\|Y_0-S_0\|_{L^2}∥QYt​−a⋆​∥L2​≤e−mt∥Y0​−S0​∥L2​.

Proof. Apply the parameter projection to the integral equation of YYY. The physical noise has zero parameter block, so its parameter remains the deterministic initial value minus the integral of the expected parameter force. The zero-score identity makes the frozen reference an admissible mean-field solution with constant parameter a⋆a_\stara⋆​. Subtract their two equations. Their common additive noise cancels. Strong monotonicity, including the deterministic-parameter expectation identities, gives the energy inequality ddt∥Yt−St∥L22≤−2m∥Yt−St∥L22\frac d{dt}\|Y_t-S_t\|_{L^2}^2\le-2m\|Y_t-S_t\|_{L^2}^2dtd​∥Yt​−St​∥L22​≤−2m∥Yt​−St​∥L22​. Multiply by e2mte^{2mt}e2mt; the derivative of the product is nonpositive. Integrating from zero to ttt gives ∥Yt−St∥L22≤e−2mt∥Y0−S0∥L22\|Y_t-S_t\|_{L^2}^2\le e^{-2mt}\|Y_0-S_0\|_{L^2}^2∥Yt​−St​∥L22​≤e−2mt∥Y0​−S0​∥L22​. Nonnegative square roots and the norm-one parameter projection finish the proof. Continuity and the supplied integral equations provide the time-integrability needed for this energy argument. □\square□

13Root-mean-square error of the full-batch scheme §

Let K=MN>0K=MN>0K=MN>0. Assume m>0m>0m>0, differentiable jointly mmm-strongly convex heterogeneous potentials with LLL-Lipschitz gradients, and a stable positive step. The optimizer a⋆a_\stara⋆​ is the actual marginal optimizer already constructed from these potentials. Supply an L2L^2L2 initial latent cloud with the stated frozen Gibbs law at a⋆a_\stara⋆​, the correct individual posterior marginals, the local domination assumptions for evidence differentiation, and independent initial posterior scores. The coordinate Brownian processes have independent scalar Euler increments, independent of the initial latent cloud. Suppose each centred score has second moment at most V0V_0V0​. These initialization, independence and regularity conditions are part of the theorem.

Claim. For the actual pointwise Euler recursion,

(E∥an−a⋆∥2)1/2≤qnR0+2mV0MN+Lm(hLdz+432dzh),q=1−mh/2,\left(\mathbb E\|a_n-a_\star\|^2\right)^{1/2}\le q^nR_0+\frac2m\sqrt{\frac{V_0}{MN}}+\frac Lm\left(h\sqrt{L d_z}+\frac43\sqrt{2d_z}\sqrt h\right),\qquad q=1-mh/2,(E∥an​−a⋆​∥2)1/2≤qnR0​+m2​MNV0​​​+mL​(hLdz​​+34​2dz​​h​),q=1−mh/2,

where R0R_0R0​ is the L2L^2L2 distance from the initial cloud to the scaled posterior cloud at a⋆a_\stara⋆​, and dzd_zdz​ is the dimension of one latent vector.

Proof. The evidence derivative at the optimizer centres the sum of posterior scores. The stipulated Gibbs initialization and independent Brownian increments furnish the stationary frozen reference used by the preceding stochastic comparison. Its frozen drift moment is bounded by Ldz\sqrt{Ld_z}Ldz​​, and the scaled physical noise has increment norm 2dzt\sqrt{2d_z}\sqrt t2dz​​t​. These facts give the three-term comparison with sampling residual K−1∑iVar⁡(si)K^{-1}\sqrt{\sum_i\operatorname{Var}(s_i)}K−1∑i​Var(si​)​. The per-score bound gives ∑iVar⁡(si)≤KV0\sum_i\operatorname{Var}(s_i)\le KV_0∑i​Var(si​)≤KV0​, hence

1K∑iVar⁡(si)≤KV0K=V0K.\frac1K\sqrt{\sum_i\operatorname{Var}(s_i)}\le\frac{\sqrt{KV_0}}K=\sqrt{\frac{V_0}K}.K1​i∑​Var(si​)​≤KKV0​​​=KV0​​​.

All factors are nonnegative and K>0K>0K>0, so taking square roots and dividing preserves the inequality. Substitute K=MNK=MNK=MN and the explicit moment constants. The pointwise and lifted recursions agree in L2L^2L2, which converts the projected norm to the displayed integral. No assertion of uniform complexity follows unless the constants stay bounded independently of particle count and step size. □\square□
